name: enrich this node: when the discussion under a node outran what was filed (long answers, few user facts), the proposal draws the missing children from the record; apply adds them; undo removes them (M189)

rounds.user: What should I look for in a grinder?
rounds.assistant: Five things. Burr type: flat burrs give a more uniform grind and clarity, conical burrs are more forgiving and quieter. Burr size: 54 mm is the entry point for espresso, 64 mm and up grinds faster and cooler. Retention: single-dosing grinders keep under 0.3 g behind, hopper grinders can hold 2–5 g of stale grounds. Adjustment: stepless lets you dial espresso precisely, stepped is easier for filter. Motor speed: slower burrs (under 1400 rpm) heat the coffee less.

rounds.user: and which ones do people actually buy?
rounds.assistant: Three tiers people settle on. Entry: the Baratza Encore ESP around 200, conical, stepped, fine for filter and okay for espresso. Mid: the DF64 around 400, 64 mm flat burrs, single-dose, stepless — the value pick for espresso. High: the Niche Zero around 700, 63 mm conical, near-zero retention, quiet; or the Eureka Mignon Specialita around 500 for a hopper machine with a timer.
Take your time — the DF64 is the usual answer for espresso at home.
